title: split-scheduler: introduce fastpath evaluator and KV heuristic fallback
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: observed end-to-end tail latency spikes when heavy KV cache churn interacts with continuous batching and the scheduler's single evaluation path. This addresses a class of regressions where the eager fast-path evaluator would return slightly out-of-spec logits under low-precision kernel fallbacks during GC-like KV churn. Design: split the scheduler's evaluation phase into two distinct evaluators: fastpath_evaluator (aggressive kernels, lower overhead) and safe_evaluator (conservative kernels, strict correctness). The scheduler now assigns requests to the fastpath by default using a runtime gating heuristic; on repeated soft failures (accuracy-check mismatches, KV lookup misses that cause cache rebuilds, or precision toggle events) requests are demoted to the safepath and a per-session KV heuristic updates to avoid oscillation. Added a KV cache heuristic module that tracks per-key miss-rate and recent rebuild windows and suppresses aggressive cache eviction when continuous batching is high. Implemented an opt-in environment flag REDWOOD_FASTPATH_SAFEGATES with three modes: off | permissive | strict. Default is permissive so we gain perf without surprising correctness regressions. Includes metrics, tracing, and a canary rollout plan. Compatibility: preserves API and config surface; no schema changes. Tests: unit tests for evaluator selection logic, integration test that replays a recorded workload with induced KV churn and asserts token-level similarity thresholds, e2e perf test results included below.

review_comments: Marco Chen: Great separation. Please add a comment explaining why the fastpath does not check kv->validity synchronously; I want to avoid future regressions where callers assume strong consistency.
Aisha Patel: Added inline docs and a unit test that ensures the fastpath observes KV validity before returning tokens. The fastpath only skips a heavyweight KV-lock in permissive mode.
Lina Ortega: Can we get perf numbers for both permissive and strict modes and a regression window? I want to see the cost of demotion under heavy load.
Aisha Patel: Attached canary run stats to the PR and summarized below. Demotion costs ~6-10% P50 token latency on a pathological trace but reduces mispredictions to zero.
Daniel Kim: Security note: ensure the safe_evaluator always uses deterministic kernels for audited deployments. Marking as requested change to add an explicit policy flag.
Aisha Patel: Added runtime/flags check and documented the default to be enabled only for enterprise compliance profiles. Updated release notes accordingly.
Lina Ortega: Approving after the perf dashboard link and CI is green.
Marco Chen: Approved. Squash merge recommended to keep history focused.
ci_checks: Unit tests: pass (fastpath and safepath suites)
Integration tests: flaky first run (timeout on kv_churn_replay), rerun passed
perf_summary: Canary workload: real customer trace with high prefix reuse and induced KV churn
Baseline (main): P50 token latency 22ms, P95 78ms, tokens/sec 540
Worst-case demotion trace: demotion increased P50 by 6-10% for affected sessions but eliminated 100% of small-output-drift regressions observed previously
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Feature gate off in prod, enabled in canary cluster for 48h
Stage 2: Permissive mode to 10% of traffic for 72h with similarity monitoring
Stage 3: Ramp to 50% if no regressions, strict mode available via config for sensitive customers
Rollback: instant toggle via REDWOOD_FASTPATH_SAFEGATES=off and rollback automation that reassigns in-flight batches to safe_evaluator
release_notes: Introduces scheduler split (fastpath/safe) and KV cache heuristics. Default gating mode is permissive. Improves token throughput and reduces tail latency while providing a conservative safepath for correctness-sensitive workloads. Operators can set REDWOOD_FASTPATH_SAFEGATES to control behavior. See docs/flags/fastpath_safegates.md for details.
